ov: Venomous snakes with long, hinged fangs that fold back against the roof of the mouth when not in use. Vipers live in most parts of the world, but not Antarctica or Australia, and most give birth to live young. The common European adder lives farther north than any other snake.

why.dg: All vipers are venomous, but the common adder is not aggressive, and its bites, though very painful, are rarely fatal.
why.h: The adder hibernates for about five to six months in Britain, and up to nine in northern Sweden.

rg: The Americas, Africa, Europe and Asia. The adder ranges from Britain across Eurasia to the Pacific, north of the Arctic Circle.
df: The adder eats mainly small mammals such as mice, voles and shrews, plus lizards, birds and amphibians.
fx: Pit vipers, such as rattlesnakes, have heat-sensing pits near their nostrils that detect warm-blooded prey.
In Britain, male adders hibernate for about 150 days a year and females for about 180.
